clue.text: Ivy gets state's North American representative to turn up

parts.note: Virginia is a US state
the Cree are a North American indigenous people

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters run from the bottom upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for representative

explanation.surface: An ivy plant is somehow given a state's North American delegate who has to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine widely called an ivy, a loose but common label for the plant.

clue.text: Definitely from St Andrews?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: belonging to a golf course, St Andrews being the famous Scottish links

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: St Andrews in Scotland is the 'home of golf', so something from there is literally from the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday assent meaning certainly, and read word by word it describes something belonging to a golf links.

clue.text: Frequently supports credit for small farm …

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word that supports another sits underneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Something often props up the credit of a smallholding, with an ellipsis carrying on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands and islands.

clue.text: … outbuildings and temporary pasture in part of Yorkshire

parts.note: barns are farm outbuildings
a ley is land sown with grass for a few years before being ploughed again

explanation.surface: Continuing the farm theme: barns and grazing land found somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNSLEY is a town in South Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnsley is a town and borough in South Yorkshire, so it is a part of that English county.

clue.text: Have permit to go by plane, then lose it!

parts.note: to let is to permit
to fly is to travel by aircraft

explanation.surface: A traveller gets permission to fly, then loses their temper anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is an idiom for erupting in anger, the same as losing your temper or losing it.

clue.text: Refuse place to get rid of stockpile

parts.note: to scrap something is to discard it
a heap is a pile of things

explanation.surface: Someone declines a place where they could clear out their hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb to decline; here it is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded rubbish, so literally a place for refuse.

clue.text: Vehicle's brought back with thanks from pilot

indicators.note: read as one unit, brought back with means the vehicle together with the thanks is returned in the opposite direction

parts.note: a van is a vehicle; the 's is read as is, a link
tas, plural of ta, British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A van returned to its depot with gratitude from the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'brought back with' as one signal covering both pieces. A satnav, short for satellite navigation, guides a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav navigates for a driver, as a pilot guides a ship into harbour.

clue.text: How to make pear juice for a media Q & A session?

definitions.meaning: read as an instruction: squeeze a well-known British variety of pear
a meeting where journalists put questions to someone

explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety, so the instruction is to press Conference pears.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is an event where reporters question a spokesperson, a media question-and-answer session.

clue.text: Fashionable mink has one consumed with anger

parts.note: in means fashionable
mink is a fur
I is the Roman numeral one
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A fashionable mink coat has someone eaten up with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate is to make someone extremely angry, so it works as the verb anger.

clue.text: Lead a meeting about Barnet

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair

explanation.surface: Running a meeting concerning Barnet, a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: Barnet Fair, hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, which is leading it.

clue.text: Outside cooking food, Tommy for one has a great time

indicators.note: one piece sits outside, wrapping round the other

parts.note: a Tommy gun is a submachine gun, so Tommy is one kind of gun

indicators.note: cooking ingredients transforms them, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A British soldier, a Tommy, enjoys himself cooking food outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy looks like the British soldier; it is the Tommy gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Good fun is an idiom for an enjoyable time, matching a great time as a noun phrase.

clue.text: A Parisian in apartment on Seine's left bank shows off

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece sitting on the end of another follows it
one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
un is French for a

indicators.note: the left side of a written word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Seine

explanation.surface: A Parisian in a flat by the Seine's Left Bank shows off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Left Bank is the bohemian district of Paris south of the Seine, which makes the selector look like a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display ostentatiously, so flaunts means shows off.

clue.text: Retired doctor's a space geek

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A retired doctor turns out to be an astronomy enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: An en (and an em) is a unit of space in typesetting, a frequent crossword source of EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerd and geek are near synonyms for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast.

clue.text: President has vocal slip welcoming Yemeni leader and causes chaos

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for president

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other
a slip is an error, so the letters fall into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Yemeni

explanation.surface: A president's verbal gaffe while hosting Yemen's leader creates diplomatic chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To play havoc is an idiom for causing disorder, so plays havoc means causes chaos.

clue.text: Patient carrier's challenge to the Queen

parts.note: to stretch someone is to challenge them
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A hospital porter's tough task in serving the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective meaning calm; it is a hospital patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is the frame on which an injured or sick person is carried.

clue.text: Notice and see about small point capably

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: one piece is placed about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see
pt is the short form of point

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe and look closely at a minor detail, done competently.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is the crossword's favourite one.
explanation.definitionFit: Adeptly means with skill, which is the same as capably.

clue.text: Stand amid Scottish mountain ferns …

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain
a rack is a stand for holding things

explanation.surface: Standing among the ferns on a Highland mountainside, with an ellipsis leading to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large coarse fern that covers hillsides, so it can stand for ferns collectively.

clue.text: One in two unions has great aims blurred over time

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece over another comes before it

parts.note: big means great

indicators.note: something blurred loses its clear shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone in two relationships finds their grand plans muddled as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist is a person married to two spouses at once, so is in two unions.

clue.text: They carry means of entry to important groups

parts.note: key means important
a ring is a group, as of spies or dealers

explanation.surface: Couriers carry passes giving access to influential circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Key rings hold keys, and keys are the usual means of entry to a building.

clue.text: … and search area for a place to shoot

parts.note: to rifle is to search through hastily
a range is an area or extent

explanation.surface: Continuing from the fern-covered hills: hunting through the area for a good spot for shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle range is a practice ground for firearms, a place where people shoot at targets.

clue.text: Days ahead for fellow taking Aussie truck round old city

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a ute is an Australian utility pickup truck
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A man plans to drive an Australian pickup around an ancient city in the coming days.
explanation.definitionFit: The future is the time still to come, the days ahead.

clue.text: Nowadays onset of diabetes in middle age is increasing

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of the calendar

indicators.note: onset of means the very start, so the first letter is taken
middle points at the central letter of the short word after it

explanation.surface: These days, diabetes appearing in middle age is becoming more common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nowadays' gives AD as the era label, not a letter pick, even though those letters sit in the middle of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting more on makes a total grow, so adding is the same as increasing.

clue.text: Storyteller picked up old instrument

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a liar tells stories, in the sense of untruths

explanation.surface: A storyteller collected an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' suggests a narrator; here it is someone telling fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a small harp of ancient Greece, an old stringed instrument.

clue.text: Care about keeping student untroubled

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
about suggests moving things around, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is a learner, so a student

explanation.surface: Concern over looking after a pupil, untroubled in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear mind or conscience is one free of worry, so clear can mean untroubled.

clue.text: Tempted to cite negligence in death

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: death is the end

indicators.note: negligence means carelessness, so the letters are carelessly shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer is tempted to blame negligence for a fatality.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed means lured or attracted, so it matches tempted as a past participle.

clue.text: Part of Guatemala is experiencing disease

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the country's name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A region of Guatemala is suffering from an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of illness or unease, close to disease in its old sense of discomfort.

clue.text: Mysterious English couple conceal revolutionary passion

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside

parts.note: two lots of E, the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a revolution turns things around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A mysterious English pair hide a revolutionary zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, which overlaps with mysterious.

clue.text: Looking back wistfully at closing building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gazes sadly at a building that is shutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as a noun, the thing being closed; it is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic describes a sentimental longing for the past, looking back wistfully.
